messages:
IncBot: INCIDENT CREATED — GPU pool exhaustion detected (severity: P1). Paging: @Maya (oncall). Auto-detect: HPA metrics missing for 3 clusters.
Maya (oncall): got the page, jumping in. seeing elevated queue length on inference-requests: ~12k pending entries.
Sam (sre): confirmed, dashboard spike at 14:31 UTC, node GPU utilization ~100% across gpu-pool-us-west, pods in Pending X/200.
Jordan (mlinfra): preliminary: HPA didn't scale because metrics-adapter returned 503s for custom.metrics.k8s.io. prom-adapter backlog visible.
Maya (oncall): is there customer impact? any 5xx from API gateway?
Alex (platform): yes — observable: router 5xxs rising, ~1.8% errors in last 5m, latency up ~400ms p95. Affected customers: some embeddings & realtime chat routes.
Carla (custsuccess): flagged two customers (acme-inc, beta-weather) reporting timeouts. I opened tickets and escalated.
Sam (sre): attaching quick logs:
```
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/metrics-adapter -c adapter | tail -n 50
E1201 14:28:11.123 adapter.go:245] failed to handle request: context deadline exceeded
W1201 14:29:02.456 adapter.go:198] queue length 8321 > threshold 8000, rejecting
```

Sam (sre): metrics-adapter restart count increased +4 in last 10m. Prometheus scrape backlog ~30m per target (monitoring graph).
Jordan (mlinfra): prometheus remote_write shows spike and then "write slowdowns". Looks like a retention compaction + disk GC on monitoring storage node caused slow scrapes. adapter falls back to returning errors.
Maya (oncall): immediate mitigation options?
Sam (sre): 1) Bump HPA minReplicas for critical inference deployments to avoid cold starvation 2) Temporarily scale up dedicated gpu-pool nodes 3) Patch adapter to increase request timeout/backoff 4) Throttle low-priority workloads (batch jobs)
Jordan (mlinfra): I can do (2) and (3). spinning up two reserved GPU nodes in us-west now (manual reserve).
Alex (platform): I'll throttle batch via label selector: cordon & evict pods with label tier=batch-gpu.
Maya (oncall): I'll patch HPA for inference-core and chat-realtime to minReplicas=4 for now. command: 
```
kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-core --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4}}' --type=merge
kubectl -n inference patch hpa chat-realtime --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4}}' --type=merge
```
Sam (sre): doing quick check: `kubectl get hpa -n inference` prints:
```
NAME             REFERENCE                  TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-core   Deployment/inference-core  0%/80%    2         50        2
chat-realtime    Deployment/chat-realtime   0%/80%    1         40        1
```
Sam (sre): patch applied to both HPAs — new minReplicas now 4.
Jordan (mlinfra): added two GPU nodes (nvidia-a100) to gpu-pool-us-west, should hit ready in ~90s. Also increased adapter timeout in deploy: `--request-timeout=60s` and bumped worker threads from 8->20. Redeploying adapter.
Maya (oncall): monitoring: queue length dropping from 12k -> 5k and Pending pods decreasing. router 5xxs down to 0.4%.
Carla (custsuccess): updated customers: telling them we are mitigating, ETA ~20m.
Sam (sre): we still see some HPA metrics lag: custom.metrics endpoints show increasing latency 200ms -> 2.5s. adapter logs show intermittent 504s from prometheus api.
Jordan (mlinfra): mitigation 2/2: Prometheus shard with GC is being rebooted by infra to recover IO. remote_write backlog clearing.
Maya (oncall): handoff note for next oncall in 30m: will need to watch adapter restarts and GPU pool autoscaler.
Sam (sre): short-term fallback: enable autoscaler fallback policy to scale by CPU-based metrics for a time window. patching autoscaler config now.
Alex (platform): throttled 18 batch pods (tier=batch-gpu) — eviction complete, freed ~4 GPUs worth of capacity.
Maya (oncall): customer impact reduced, but some long-running requests still queued — enabling request queuing priority: mark realtime routes priority=high to preempt batch.
Jordan (mlinfra): Prometheus node back online, scrape latency recovering. adapter error rate trending to 0.
Sam (sre): observing GPUs now ~75% avg, queue ~900. Autoscaler accepted metrics and triggered scale from HPA to add 6 pods — new pods scheduling.
Maya (oncall): great. I'll create follow-up action items: postmortem, add more robust adapter retries, increase Prometheus storage IO SLOs, add a fallback metric for autoscaler.
Carla (custsuccess): I've sent customer updates with root-cause summary and compensation timeline.
IncBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — GPU exhaustion mitigated, services restored to normal. Total incident duration ~38 minutes.
Sam (sre): notes to include in postmortem: root cause = Prometheus shard IO GC caused scrape slowdowns -> metrics-adapter returned errors -> HPA saw no metrics -> no scaling -> GPU pool exhausted. Contributing: no HPA fallback metric, batch workloads not preempted, adapter timeouts too low.
Jordan (mlinfra): next steps I'm taking: increase adapter resiliency, add caching for custom metrics, implement a short-lived probe metric so HPA can fallback to approx load.
Maya (oncall): handing off to night team. full runbook updated with explicit steps for manual minReplica bump & node reserve.
Carla (custsuccess): closing out customer communication thread, will follow up after postmortem.
Sam (sre): Adding tags: gpu, autoscale, metrics-adapter, prometheus, customer-impact.
Maya (oncall): thanks team. good catch on the adapter backlog. I'm logging this for the postmortem meeting tomorrow. :thumbsup:
